statement: Whenever the function returns a result r for input (nums, k), r is the maximum value of x over all x for which a valid index sequence of length x exists, where an increasing index sequence (i_0, i_1, ..., i_{x-1}) with 0 <= i_0 < i_1 < ... < i_{x-1} < len(nums) is called valid iff x <= 1 or, for every j with 0 <= j <= x-2, (nums[i_j] + nums[i_{j+1}]) mod k = (nums[i_0] + nums[i_1]) mod k. Equivalently, r is the length of a longest valid subsequence of nums.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 2, len(nums) <= 1000, and 1 <= k <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 10^7. Here a mod k denotes the least non-negative remainder of a modulo k, so 0 <= a mod k < k.

statement: On every input satisfying the preconditions the function returns a result; it does not fail (no 64-bit overflow, no out-of-bounds indexing, no panic).
preconditions: len(nums) >= 2, len(nums) <= 1000, and 1 <= k <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 10^7.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, 2 <= r <= len(nums).
preconditions: len(nums) >= 2, len(nums) <= 1000, and 1 <= k <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 10^7.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, there exists a valid index sequence of length r: indices 0 <= i_0 < i_1 < ... < i_{r-1} < len(nums) such that for every j with 0 <= j <= r-2, (nums[i_j] + nums[i_{j+1}]) mod k equals (nums[i_0] + nums[i_1]) mod k.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 2, len(nums) <= 1000, and 1 <= k <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 10^7.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, every valid index sequence has length at most r: for every increasing index sequence 0 <= i_0 < i_1 < ... < i_{x-1} < len(nums) whose consecutive pair sums (nums[i_j] + nums[i_{j+1}]) mod k are all equal, we have x <= r.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 2, len(nums) <= 1000, and 1 <= k <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 10^7.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, if the whole index sequence (0, 1, ..., len(nums)-1) is valid — that is, all the values (nums[j] + nums[j+1]) mod k for 0 <= j <= len(nums)-2 are equal to each other — then r = len(nums).
preconditions: len(nums) >= 2, len(nums) <= 1000, and 1 <= k <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 10^7.

statement: Whenever the function returns r on (nums, k) and r2 on (nums2, k), if nums[i] mod k = nums2[i] mod k for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), then r = r2.
preconditions: nums and nums2 each satisfy: len >= 2, len <= 1000, and all entries in [1, 10^7]; 1 <= k <= 1000; len(nums) = len(nums2).

statement: Whenever the function returns r on (nums, k) and r2 on (sub, k), we have r2 <= r.
preconditions: nums satisfies len(nums) >= 2, len(nums) <= 1000, entries in [1, 10^7]; k in [1, 1000]; sub satisfies len(sub) >= 2, entries in [1, 10^7]; and sub is a subsequence of nums: there are indices 0 <= j_0 < j_1 < ... < j_{m-1} < len(nums) with m = len(sub) and sub[t] = nums[j_t] for all 0 <= t < m.

statement: Whenever the function returns r on (nums, k) and r2 on (nums2, k), we have r <= r2 <= r + 1.
preconditions: nums satisfies len(nums) >= 2, len(nums) <= 999, entries in [1, 10^7]; k in [1, 1000]; v in [1, 10^7]; and nums2 is nums with v appended at the end (len(nums2) = len(nums)+1, nums2[i] = nums[i] for 0 <= i < len(nums), and nums2[len(nums)] = v).

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r >= max over a with 0 <= a < k of cnt(a), where cnt(a) is the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(nums) and nums[i] mod k = a.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 2, len(nums) <= 1000, and 1 <= k <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 10^7.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r <= M1 + M2, where cnt(a) for 0 <= a < k is the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(nums) and nums[i] mod k = a, and M1 >= M2 are the two largest values among the counts cnt(0), cnt(1), ..., cnt(k-1) (when k = 1, take M2 = 0).
preconditions: len(nums) >= 2, len(nums) <= 1000, and 1 <= k <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 10^7.
